column2: A battle of showering weapons and missiles took place with Hari and the Daitya's son; the glorious Hari killed that enemy on the northern bank.
On the Ganga is the Narasimha tirtha, renowned in the three worlds; bathing, giving and the like there crush the grip of all sins.
It always protects all, and holds back old age and death. As no god among all the gods is equal to Hari,
so that tirtha is the best of all tirthas. A man who bathes at that tirtha should worship Nrihari.
In heaven, on earth or below, nothing is hard to obtain for him. There, sage Narada, are eight great tirthas beginning with this;
the wise say each separately gives the fruit of ten million tirthas. By remembering whose name even without faith all sins are destroyed,
where Nrisimha himself always dwells in person — who can describe the fruit born of serving that tirtha here?
As no god anywhere is greater than Nrihari, so no tirtha anywhere is equal to the Nrisimha tirtha.
He looked at her at night, unclothed and astonished, the great one. In the meantime the king went out to battle against enemies.
Having conquered them he returned again to the well-honoured world of the gods; and that great king, coming back, with Vasishtha as priest,
hearing of Urvashi's departure, was then full of grief; he did not offer oblations, nor eat, nor hear, nor see.
In the meantime the priest awakened with reasonable words the best of kings, who was in a state like death:

She is dead today, great king; do not suffer, great-minded one. Thus placed, let not inauspicious, swift things touch you.
brahmapuran:151:12	You do not know women's hearts, great-minded one; they are like jackals' hearts; therefore, king, do not grieve.
brahmapuran:151:13	Who in the world, lord of kings, has not been deceived by women? Deceitfulness, cruelty, fickleness, bad conduct —
brahmapuran:151:14	these being natural to them, how can they be causes of happiness? Who has not been killed by time? What petitioner has gained respect?
brahmapuran:151:15	Who has not been whirled by fortune? Who has not been broken by women? Like a dream and illusion, king, with minds drenched in pride,
brahmapuran:151:16	for whose happiness are women? Knowing this, be free of fever. Leaving aside Shankara, Vishnu or the Gautami, great-minded one, there is no other refuge for the suffering in the three worlds.
Hearing this, the king then forcibly put aside his grief, and Aila, exceedingly righteous, stayed in the midst of the Gautami.
There he diligently worshipped Shiva, the god Janardana, Brahma, the Sun, the Ganga, the gods and others.
A creature who in distress does not serve holy places and deities, subject to time, what state will he reach?
So, having the Lord as his sole refuge, eager to serve the Gautami, he attained supreme faith and turned away from reliance on worldly existence.
He performed many sacrifices with officiating priests and abundant fees; he became an island of the Vedas, so that place is called Yajnadvipa.
On full-moon nights Urvashi always comes there. A man who circumambulates that island
has circumambulated the earth with its seas and sky. Remembrance of the Vedas and remembrance of sacrifices occur there.
The righteous man who does so there obtains the fruit of Vedic sacrifices. That should be known as Aila-tirtha, and also as Pururava.
It is also Vasishtha's, and it is called Nimnabheda (the breaking of lowness). For the king Aila there was nothing low in any of his acts.
That lowness, behaviour with all one's being toward Urvashi, was also broken by Vasishtha and by the Ganga.
Thus the breaking of lowness occurred, granting success in seen and unseen desires. There, they say, are seven hundred virtuous holy places.
Bathing and giving at them grant the fruit of all sacrifices. One who, having bathed at Nimnabheda, sees these gods
has no lowness here or hereafter; having obtained complete elevation he rejoices in heaven like Shakra.
Having studied all the other sciences too, from Jiva, I (Moon) shall do honour to the teacher, Chandra told Jiva (Brihaspati). Then Brihaspati, joyful, said to his pupil the Moon:
My beloved Tara, radiant like Rati, knows (the subject).
To ask her, the Moon then went inside the house; seeing Tara, moon-faced, he seized her by the hand.
Out of greed he dragged her by force to his own house. The wise, intelligent, sense-conquering treasure of steadiness remains so only
until bound by the aguru-fragrance of women's eyes and speech; and especially on seeing a woman, long-eyed, alone —
whose mind does not come under the sway of desires? Hence one should never look at another man's (wife).
A family wife, afraid of loss of virtue, must act in secret; knowing it from his attendants, he rose suddenly and went out.
Seeing that wicked act, Brihaspati of noble mind cursed him in anger, taunting him with unpleasant words.
Seeing his beloved wronged by another, who could endure it? Jiva the god fought with the Moon in rage.
The Moon is not killed by curses, nor by weapons empowered by gods, nor by mantras composed by Brihaspati.
Then the Moon, having taken that Tara and established her in his house, enjoyed her for many years, as he did Rohini, fearless.
He was not defeated then by gods, by anger, curses or mantras, by kings or sages, nor by conciliation, division or punishment.
When the teacher could not get his wife back by all efforts, Jiva, with all means exhausted, recalled statecraft:

The wise man, putting insult first and pride behind, accomplishes his own aim; to lose one's own aim is folly.
brahmapuran:152:17	For men who know, the fruit is to be attained by some means; those vainly proud, bewildered, quickly perish.
Having thus decided, the wise one went to Shukra and told him; Kavi (Shukra), knowing him come, welcomed him with honour.
When he was seated, well rested and duly honoured, the teacher of the Daityas asked the reason for his coming.
Even the best enemies do not turn away from one come to the house; so he told him in detail from the beginning of the abduction of his wife.
Hearing Brihaspati's words, Kavi, filled with anger, considered it an offence of his pupil the Moon, Narada. Hearing this transgression, Kavi then said in anger:

I shall then eat, drink, sleep and speak, brother, when I bring back your wife who is being afflicted by another.
brahmapuran:152:23	Having brought her, worshipped Bhava, and cursed the Moon, betrayer of his teacher, afterwards I shall eat, mighty-armed one; hear my word, lord of planets.
Having said so to Jiva, the Daitya teacher went; having propitiated Shiva with effort, he obtained supreme capability.
Having obtained various boons from Shankara, worshipped with devotion — what is hard to get for embodied beings here by Shiva's grace?
Shukra went with Jiva to where the Moon was with Tara and cursed him loudly: "Moon, hear my words:
since you, sinner, from pride did an exceedingly sinful act, you shall become a leper." Thus Kavi cursed the Moon in rage.
Scorched by Kavi's curse, the deer-marked one at once met decay; who does not meet destruction, a betrayer of teacher, master or friend?
The Moon gave up Tara, and Kavi took her; Shukra also summoned the gods, sages and ancestors,
rivers and streams of many kinds, herbs and devoted wives, and then began to ask for the atonement for Tara's conduct.
Then the Shruti said to the gods: "In the Gautami, with devotion — let Tara bathe with Jiva, and she will be purified.
This supreme secret must not be told to just anyone; in all states here the Gautami is the refuge of men."
Tara did so, bathing with her husband as prescribed; there was a rain of flowers and shouts of victory arose.
The gods gave again, and men and kings giving again, making a truth, gave back the Brahmin's wife.
Having given back the Brahmin's wife, made faultless by the gods, all was well there; therefore it is a holy place, great sage.

Having given back the Brahmin's wife, made faultless by the gods, all was well there; therefore, great sage, it became a holy place, destroying the mass of all sins, granting all desires; delight and welfare came to the gods and the foes of the Asuras.
Brihaspati, Shukra and especially Tara attained supreme delight; the teacher then spoke to the Ganga:

You, Gautami, are always to be worshipped by all, giver of liberation to all; especially when I stand in Leo you purify the three worlds,
brahmapuran:152:39	best of rivers, joined with all holy places. Whatever holy places there are in heaven, earth or the nether world, they will come to bathe in you when I am in Leo, mother.
brahmapuran:152:40	Blessed, fame-giving, life-giving, increasing health and prosperity, producing fortune and lordship is the holy place named Ananda.
Gautama says there are five thousand holy places there; by remembering or reciting them one is always joined with what is desired.
Here Nandi, dwelling by Shiva, constantly moves on the Ganga bank, being Dharma itself, so it is called Nandi-bank. That holy place is also Ananda, because it increases all delight.
They all became glad, always following Rama. Then after a few days, from outcasts, a disapproving
word was heard; he gave up that pregnant one, not born of a womb. Those of exalted family do not tolerate even a false slander.
Lakshmana, weeping, abandoned the blameless, weeping Sita near the hermitage of the chief of sages Valmiki.
The command of elders must not be transgressed, he thought, and did so out of fear. Then, after a few days had passed, the king's son
Rama, with Lakshmana, was initiated for the horse-sacrifice. There came both the famed sons of Rama,
Lava and Kusha, renowned, singers like two Naradas, who sang the whole Ramayana, with fine voices like Gandharvas.
Singing the whole story of Rama, they approached the sacrificial ground; the princes were then recognised by signs:
These two heroes, sons of Rama, are the sons of Vaidehi. Rama brought them and consecrated the sons in due order,
placed them on his lap and embraced them again and again. For embodied beings worn by the sorrows of worldly existence, without recourse,
the embrace of a son is the supreme cause of rest here. Repeatedly embracing his two sons, he embraces and kisses them again and again,
and meditates on something within, and sighs repeatedly. In the meantime the Rakshasas dwelling in Lanka arrived,
Sugriva and Hanuman, Angada and Jambavan, and all the other monkeys, led by Vibhishana.
They came and reached the king seated on the throne; not seeing Sita, Hanuman and Angada, golden-armleted, said:
Where has the mother, not born of a womb, gone? Only Rama is seen here. The doorkeepers said, "She has been abandoned by Rama."

While the world-guardians looked on, and the noble lady spoke of it, Sita, purified in fire — yet the king, unrestrained,
brahmapuran:154:26	because of worldly rumours, abandons his beloved. Saying "We shall die," the two went again to the Gautami.
Rama came behind them with the residents of Ayodhya, and having reached the Gautami there, they performed supreme austerity,
remembering again and again and sighing for that Sita, mother of the world, free of reliance on worldly existence, eager to serve the Gautami.
Rama himself, lord of the three worlds, with his younger brother, arrived and bathed in the Gautami, intent on worship of Shiva.
Surrounded by a thousand, he gave up all anguish; the place where that event occurred is called Sahasrakunda.
Ten other holy places there give all aims; bathing and giving there grant the fruit of a thousand.
Where on the bank of the glorious Gautami Vasishtha and the other lords of sages had performed an oblation that saves from all calamities and destroys sin,
in the thousand kundas, by streams of wealth, that great ascetic obtained all desires sought.
By the grace of the mother river Gautami, destroyer of Rakshasas, that holy place named Sahasrakunda, of great fruit, came to be.
That is Kapila-sangama, destroying the mass of all sins; there from the water of the gift a river named Kapila arose.
By the gift even of a fertile land a cow-gift is best; the sage, making an exchange, protected the world.
The tirtha where that happened is called Gotirtha; the wise say there are a hundred merit-giving holy places there.
By bathing and giving there one obtains the fruit of land-gift; they know it as Kapila-sangama, joined with the Ganga.
Seeing her, the glorious king entered the Ganga bank; seeing her, the king, with a voice choked with joy, then addressed all the monkeys led by Hanuman, sage:

By her power, monkeys, my father the lord, freed from all sins, went to heaven.
brahmapuran:157:10	She is the mother of every creature, granting enjoyment, and also liberation; she kills even terrible sins. What river here is equal to her?
brahmapuran:157:11	Sins are always destroyed, and by her power enemies become friends: Vibhishana constantly shows friendship, Sita was regained, and Hanuman is my kinsman,
brahmapuran:157:12	Lanka was broken and the Rakshasas with their host slain by serving her — she whom Gautama obtained, having worshipped the best of gods, Shiva the refuge, with his matted locks.
brahmapuran:157:13	She is the mother of all desires, destroyer of even inauspicious things, uniquely skilled in purifying the world, today seen in person, the mother of rivers.
brahmapuran:157:14	With body, speech and mind I always go to the Ganga, the refuge, for refuge.
Hearing this word of the king, all the monkeys bathed there, and each worshipped her by rule with many flowers and with offerings of all the worlds.
The king, having duly worshipped Sharva and praised him with words suited to every feeling, and all the monkeys, glad, danced and sang likewise.
The great-souled one passed the night happily, surrounded by loving, affectionate followers, and gave up all sorrow caused by enemies; what is not obtained by serving the Gautami?
Astonished, he looks at the body of his servants and praises the Godavari, delighted; honouring the whole body of attendants, Rama obtained some unique joy.
Even today we are not satisfied at this tirtha; let us live here for some time, and stay here four more nights, and then go back to Ayodhya.
The monkeys agreed to his word, and likewise four more nights; having worshipped the god, Lord of all, he went to the tirtha dear to his brother,
named Siddheshvara, famed in the world, by whose power the mighty ten-faced one (Ravana) was... Thus they stayed five days, each worshipping the linga he had installed.
There Hanuman, son of the Wind, follower of the king, served; as they were going, the king of kings said to Hanuman: "Dismiss all the lingas
installed by me, by knowers of the best mantras, and by others, servants of Shankara; worship should not be removed by another Shankara; ah, an external thing must be arranged for Bhava.
Those who stand well in disrespect of it, who, lacking faith, having performed worship of the Shiva-linga, do not do their duty — they are born in sword-leaf forests and the like,
and are cooked by Yama's servants, as is fitting, in all the hells." At Rama's command the Wind's son went but could not uproot it with his arms.
Then, wishing to seize it with his tail, he wrapped the linga but, giving up his desire, could not; this was a great wonder to the monkey-lords and likewise to the king.
What wise man would move a linga of Maheshvara which has acquired great power? Seeing it immovable, the king, the great-souled hero, suddenly went away.
Then, having invited Brahmins and performed worship and circumambulation, Ramachandra with a purified, extremely pure heart bowed to all those lingas.
Thereupon this holy place was served by all the chief residents of Kishkindha; merely by bathing here even great sins are destroyed, no doubt.
And again he bowed to the Ganga with devotion, saying "Be gracious to me, mother Gautami," repeatedly, his mind astonished, gazing and bowing to the Gautami.
From then on the gods call this exceedingly holy place Kishkindha-tirtha. One who recites or remembers or hears it with devotion is freed from sin; what then of those who bathe and give?

What shall we do? What is the way here? Shall we remain in austerity alone? Tell us the means, best of Brahmins; you are surely the eldest by austerity.
brahmapuran:158:14	You are the knower among knowers, Brahmin, the best of speakers; you are tranquil, always among the restrained, compassionate and doing good,
brahmapuran:158:15	without anger and without hatred; therefore say what you wish to say. The proud, the merciless, those without service of the teacher, untruthful, cruel, do not know the truth.
Agastya, after meditating a moment, slowly said to them all:

You are peaceful-souled, creators made by Brahma; your austerity was not sufficient; recall the cause of pride.
brahmapuran:158:18	Those made earlier by Brahma who went away prosper in happiness; those who went to search again became the Angirases.
brahmapuran:158:19	You too, going in time, slowly going, will surely become greater than the Prajapati.
brahmapuran:158:20	Go from here to practise austerity at the Ganga, purifier of the three worlds; there is no other means in worldly existence without the Ganga, dear to Shiva.
brahmapuran:158:21	In the hermitage there, in a holy place, you will worship the giver of knowledge; that very wise one will cut off all your doubt, since success nowhere comes to anyone without a good teacher.
They said to the best of sages: "Who is called the giver of knowledge? Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara, or Aditya or the Moon,
Agni or Varuna, who is the giver of knowledge, best of sages?" Agastya said again, "Let this giver of knowledge be heard:
That which is water is said to be fire; that which is fire is called the Sun; that which is the Sun is Vishnu; and that which is Vishnu is the Sun-god.
That which is Brahma is Rudra; that which is Rudra is all of that. He for whom all that is knowledge is here praised as the giver of knowledge.
Guides, instigators, expounders, teachers and givers of the body — there are many teachers; of them the giver of knowledge is great.

That is the knowledge spoken of here by which difference is destroyed. The one non-dual Shambhu is called by names such as Indra, Mitra and Agni; Brahmins speak of many for the sake of favours for the confused."
Hearing the sage's words, singing verses, five of them went to the northern Ganga and five went to the southern.
Worshipping, as prescribed, the gods named by Agastya, seated in seats especially, contemplating the truth,
all the hosts of gods were pleased with them, sage; the creatorship that was ordained at the yuga's beginning by the womb of the universe (Brahma),
for the removal of unrighteousness, establishment of the Vedas, the benefit of the worlds, and the accomplishment of dharma, desire and wealth —
creatorship of the worlds is desired in determining the meaning of Purana, Smriti, Veda and Dharmashastra; you will be of such form.
Prajapati-hood will come to them slowly, in order; when unrighteousness arises and the Vedas are defeated,
then the future Vyasas arise from them, in distress of the Vedas; whenever decline of dharma and of the Veda is seen,
then those Vyasas will be helpers. Wherever their place of austerity is, the excellent bank of the Ganga,
there Shiva, Vishnu, I, the Sun, Agni and the waters, all, are always present.
Nothing is more purifying than these, nothing greater than these anywhere; having assumed these forms, the Supreme Brahman alone.
Shiva, all-pervading, whose nature is all, bearing the form of all states of being, especially in that holy place out of compassion for all creatures,
followed by all the gods, becomes the bestower of grace on them. Those should be known as Dharma-Vyasas and likewise Veda-Vyasas."
